Yes—very likely.

At **10.8° above the eastern horizon**, the Moon is geometrically well above the horizon, and at **about 60% illuminated** it is bright and conspicuous. With the Sun **50° below the horizon**, the sky is fully dark, and clear conditions strongly favor visibility. Its distance is unremarkable for naked-eye viewing.

Look **roughly east**, at azimuth **86°**, about **one fist-width at arm’s length above the horizon**. Unless buildings, mountains, trees, or local cloud/haze block that low part of the sky, you should be able to spot it easily. In Anchorage, terrain toward the east is the main practical concern.
